requirement:
Authoring MUST use the `[authoring]` sections of the shared user configuration
and the selected workspace's `habeas.toml`, refining
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections` for the authoring feature.
{cite}`requirements.configuration.user_location`
{cite}`requirements.configuration.structure`
Assessing a subject with `habeas author`, singly or in a batch that needs at
least one assessment, MUST require an `[authoring]` section in at least one of
these files; either section MAY be absent. No other operation requires the
section, including a batch with no assessments needed and the operations in
{cite}`requirements.authoring.deterministic_validation`.
It MUST support named configurations, workspace defaults, and a user-local
selection for each project. Credential-source references SHOULD be used;
explicit credentials MUST be supported under {cite}`requirements.authoring.credentials`.
{cite}`requirements.configuration.workspace_location`
{cite}`requirements.configuration.workspace_structure`
rationale:
**Gaps found.** Several obligations are implemented and tested in substance, but the marking is incomplete, and no `{fixme}` acknowledges it.

**Obligations and the code that carries them out**
- **Use the `[authoring]` sections of the user config and the workspace `habeas.toml`.** `resolve_authoring` (src/config.rs:960) loads both files. `resolve_authoring_with_workspace_from` (src/config.rs:996) reads `authoring` from each. Both functions carry `{impl}` references to the subject. Tests: `authoring_uses_nearest_workspace_configuration_without_a_user_file` (workspace only) and `Fixture::new` (user file only) in tests/authoring_cli.rs.
- **`habeas author` with at least one assessment needed requires an `[authoring]` section in one of the files, and either may be absent.** The check `authoring.is_none() && local.is_none()` returns the "no authoring configuration" error (src/config.rs). It is tested at the unit level by `explicit_project_and_default_selections_choose_whole_configs` in tests/configuration.rs, which asserts the message. That test carries no `{test}` reference to the subject.
- **A batch with no assessments needed must not require the section.** `run_batch` (src/authoring/batch.rs:78) has `if subjects.is_empty() { return Ok(outcome); }` before `config::resolve_authoring`. This is the decision the subject specifies. It is tested by `batch_fills_evidence_preserves_current_records_and_reauthors_only_changed_inputs`, which runs `author --all` with an invalid and then a missing user config and expects success.
- **Named configurations, workspace defaults, and a user-local selection for each project.** The selection precedence in `resolve_authoring_with_workspace_from` covers explicit, project, workspace default, then user default. It is tested by `workspace_defaults_and_configs_combine_with_existing_user_selections`, which carries a `{test}` reference to the subject.
- **Explicit credentials supported, credential-source references preferred.** These are handled under `requirements.authoring.credentials`, and `authoring_uses_nearest_workspace_configuration_without_a_user_file` exercises a literal `api_key`.
- **No other operation requires the section.** Validation, status, and rendering never call `resolve_authoring`.

**Marking gaps (code and tests the subject covers but does not reference)**
1. `run_batch` (src/authoring/batch.rs:78–97) implements the "batch with no assessments needed does not require authoring configuration" clause. It has a comment saying so, but its `{impl}` list does not include `requirements.authoring.configuration`. Per the marking rule, this is an implementation gap.
2. `batch_fills_evidence_preserves_current_records_and_reauthors_only_changed_inputs` (tests/authoring_batch.rs:478) verifies that clause, but it has no `{test}` reference to the subject.
3. `explicit_project_and_default_selections_choose_whole_configs` (tests/configuration.rs:251) verifies the "no authoring configuration" requirement, but it has no `{test}` reference to the subject.
4. `configured_assessment` (src/authoring/mod.rs:444) is the single-subject `habeas author` path that makes the section required by calling `resolve_authoring`. It has no reference to the subject. This one is weaker, since it only calls the implementing code.

These gaps are unacknowledged: I found no `{fixme}` against the subject.

text: :::{req} configuration
Authoring MUST use the `[authoring]` sections of the shared user configuration
and the selected workspace's `habeas.toml`, refining
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections` for the authoring feature.
{cite}`requirements.configuration.user_location`
{cite}`requirements.configuration.structure`
Assessing a subject with `habeas author`, singly or in a batch that needs at
least one assessment, MUST require an `[authoring]` section in at least one of
these files; either section MAY be absent. No other operation requires the
section, including a batch with no assessments needed and the operations in
{cite}`requirements.authoring.deterministic_validation`.
It MUST support named configurations, workspace defaults, and a user-local
selection for each project. Credential-source references SHOULD be used;
explicit credentials MUST be supported under {cite}`requirements.authoring.credentials`.
{cite}`requirements.configuration.workspace_location`
{cite}`requirements.configuration.workspace_structure`
:::{req} user_location
Habeas MUST locate its per-user configuration at
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/habeas/config.toml` on Unix when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is an absolute,
nonempty path, otherwise at `$HOME/.config/habeas/config.toml`. On Windows it MUST
use `%APPDATA%/habeas/config.toml`. `HOME` and `APPDATA` MUST likewise be
absolute, nonempty paths to be used. If no usable base directory can be
determined, an operation requiring user configuration MUST fail with an
explanatory diagnostic naming the variable.
The same user configuration MUST be usable across projects. Its location MUST
NOT be selected relative to the current project or changed by project settings.
User-local preferences for a project MAY remain in the user configuration;
workspace settings MUST use `habeas.toml` under
{cite}`requirements.configuration.workspace_location`.
:::{req} structure
The user configuration file MUST be UTF-8 TOML serializing UserConfig. It MUST
contain `version = 1` and MAY contain the documented feature tables. The common
root MUST contain only the schema version and those feature tables; feature
settings MUST NOT occupy unscoped root keys. A user file containing only
`version = 1` MUST be valid common configuration.
Workspace configuration MUST follow {cite}`requirements.configuration.workspace_structure`.
The absence of an optional feature section MUST be distinguishable
from that feature's explicit settings and interpreted according to its own
requirements.
:::{req} deterministic_validation
Ordinary evidence validation, status inspection, and book rendering MUST continue
to check evidence using the existing rules without invoking models, contacting
providers, or requiring authoring configuration or credentials. Missing or stale
evidence MUST remain a validation failure rather than trigger authoring.
:::{req} credentials
Bedrock configurations MAY supply `credentials` containing nonempty
`access_key_id`, `secret_access_key`, and optional nonempty `session_token`.
Ollama configurations MAY supply a nonempty `api_key`. Habeas MUST reject a
Bedrock record combining explicit credentials with `aws_profile`, and an Ollama
record combining `api_key` with `api_key_env`.
Explicit credentials MUST be passed directly to the selected provider without
changing process environment variables or writing credential files. Saved
explicit values MUST round-trip; credentials resolved from profiles or the
environment MUST NOT be serialized back. Debug output, configuration diagnostics,
usage records, and initial prompts MUST NOT include credential values. TOML
diagnostics MUST NOT echo credential-containing source lines. A configuration
file containing explicit credentials MAY be read as source; its credential
values MUST be redacted under {cite}`requirements.authoring.redaction`.
Validation MUST report a workspace `habeas.toml` present in the Git index that
contains explicit credentials, naming the file and the credential fields and
recommending credential-source references, because committed credentials leak.
Documentation MUST discourage literal credentials in workspace files and
recommend AWS profiles or environment-variable references. Examples MUST use
placeholders and explain that workspace files may be committed or read as source
when explicitly allowed.
:::{req} workspace_location
Habeas MUST search from its invocation directory upward for the nearest enclosing
`habeas.toml`. It MUST use that file alone, without merging ancestor workspace
files. A library operation given a project root MUST search from that root unless
its current directory is inside the project, in which case it MUST start there.
The directory containing the selected file defines the base for its relative
paths; it does not replace the Cargo and mdBook project root. A missing file MUST
mean absent workspace settings. Discovery MUST report unreadable candidate files
rather than silently selecting an ancestor. Loading MUST NOT create the file.
:::{req} workspace_structure
`habeas.toml` MUST serialize WorkspaceConfig as UTF-8 TOML with `version = 1`.
Its supported feature tables are `[authoring]` and `[evidence]`; either MAY be
absent. Unknown keys, unsupported versions, and invalid field types MUST produce
a diagnostic identifying the file and setting. Invalid TOML, including content
that is not UTF-8, MUST produce a diagnostic identifying the file, with the line
and column of a syntax error.
Features MUST define their own data structures and loading rules under
{cite}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`. A file containing only
`version = 1` MUST be valid. Habeas settings MUST NOT require a `[habeas]` table
inside `book.toml`.
